newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Arab Investment plans to raise capital to $400m.
newsitem.headline: Arab Investment plans to raise capital to $400m.

text.p: The Arab Investment Company (TAIC) said on Sunday it would review proposals to raise its paid-in capital to $400 million from $300 million.
A company statement said its board of directors would meet in Cairo next week to discuss "a proposal to raise the company's capital from $300 million to $400 million". It gave no further details.
Riyadh-based TAIC said the board would also discuss requests from Algeria and Lebanon to join the company.
Its current shareholders are Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Sudan, Egypt, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Syria, Iraq, Jordan, Tunisia, Morocco, Libya Oman and Yemen.
TAIC posted a $28 million profit in 1996, up from $18.4 million in 1995. It was established in 1974 by 15 Arab countries to invest money in Arab projects.
